To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the MI-E is a safe and effective device to augment coughing in patients with ALS.
the mechanical insufflation-exsufflation (MI-E) device was not more effective than the breath-stacking method in reducing chest infections in ALS patients with respiratory failure.

there were no statistically significant differences between the breath-stacking and mechanical insufflator exsufflator (MI-E) groups in terms of chest infections, hospital admissions, quality of life (QoL) or survival, although the breath-stacking method may be more effective for cough augmentation in patients who are unable to use a mechanical insufflator.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a mechanical device for the augmentation of cough in patients with respiratory insufficiency.

developing a new method of cough augmentation in patients who have a poor cough, such as those with amyotrophic Lateral sclerosis (ALS), and to compare it with a standard method of cough augmentation, breath stacking.

the use of mechanical insufflation-exsufflation (MI-E) as a first-line intervention to augment cough in patients with ALS, in whom there is a risk of developing chest infections and who meet the criteria to commence non-invasive ventilation (NIV).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the breath stacking technique and the MI-E device are equally efficacious in the management of respiratory failure in ALS patients.
there are no significant differences in the outcome of patients with ALS who were randomized to the MI-E or breath-stacking technique.

the breath-stacking and MI-E techniques are comparable in terms of the efficacy of cough augmentation, the frequency of chest infection, duration of hospitalization, duration of antibiotic treatment, survival and quality of life in patients with ALS.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the breath-stacking method is a simple and effective method for volume recruitment and augmentation of cough in patients with ALS.
there is no evidence to suggest that the MI-E is more effective than the breath-stacking cough augmentation technique.

the breath-stacking method is a simple technique that can be easily learnt by patients and carers, is inexpensive, and is effective for volume recruitment and effective cough augmentation in patients who are able to perform a maximal inspiratory effort.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the breath-stacking and MI-E techniques are comparable and both can be recommended for patients with ALS.
the breath-stacking method of cough augmentation can be used as an effective and safe alternative for cough augmentation in ALS patients.
the breath-stacking method is an acceptable alternative to MI-E, and it should be considered for the first-line intervention in patients with ALS.
